name: The Smile
label: XL
lede: Two-fifths of Radiohead and the drummer from Sons of Kemet, who played Glastonbury before anyone outside the room knew they existed, then made a record that Pitchfork scored 8.6.

eras.title: Radiohead, and the day jobs
eras.text: Yorke and Greenwood spend thirty-odd years inside one of the most closely watched bands in Britain, and keep building side lives: film scores, solo records, and for Skinner a jazz band of his own.

years.h: [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] start in Abingdon as On A Friday
years.p: The band is named for its rehearsal day. It becomes Radiohead in 1991 after signing with EMI.

years.h: In Rainbows goes out with a pay-what-you-want price
years.p: [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] release the album digitally and let buyers choose the price, Yorke's most public argument with the record business.
years.xp:
Yorke has been blunt about labels over the years. Wikipedia quotes him: "I like the people at our record company, but the time is at hand when you have to ask why anyone needs one."

The habit of doing things their own way carries over to The Smile, who release through XL and Self Help Tapes.

years.cap: Thom Yorke and Johnny Greenwood performing with The Smile at The Factory in Deep Ellum… · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Tom Skinner · Wikipedia: Jonny Greenwood
years.h: Greenwood scores The Master and meets Skinner in the room
years.p: Tom Skinner plays on [[Jonny Greenwood|e9fcfbbf-1743-4f73-8744-ada8da7394ea]]'s score for Paul Thomas Anderson's The Master. That's where the two first work together.
years.xp:
Greenwood has scored Anderson's films since There Will Be Blood (2007) and later picks up Oscar nominations for Phantom Thread and The Power of the Dog.

The Master is the connection Wikipedia names for how Skinner ends up in The Smile years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sons of Kemet · Wikipedia: Tom Skinner
years.h: Skinner's other band: [[Sons of Kemet|fee950a2-e68c-4e76-b1ae-ff6efdf68b11]] release Burn
years.p: Shabaka Hutchings' group, with Skinner on drums, formed in London in 2011 and puts out Burn on Naim.
years.xp:
Sons of Kemet use a saxophone, a tuba and two drummers. They win Best Jazz Act at the 2013 MOBO Awards, and their 2018 album Your Queen Is a Reptile is nominated for the Mercury Prize.

Skinner also runs a band called Hello Skinny, which releases an album in 2012 and Watermelon Sun in 2017.

years.h: Yorke's solo year: Suspiria, then Anima
years.p: [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]] scores the 2018 Suspiria remake without Nigel Godrich, then releases the solo album Anima in 2019.
years.xp:
Before that he'd led [[Atoms for Peace|9e299bee-d7e2-49f3-8cd7-d6b28ab204d1]] (Amok, 2013) and put Tomorrow's Modern Boxes out through BitTorrent in 2014.

Wikipedia reports Anima is his first chart-topper on Billboard's Dance/Electronic chart.

eras.title: A band nobody's heard
eras.text: Greenwood and Skinner start trading ideas, Yorke joins, and pandemic lockdown does the rest. The trio agrees not to talk about it.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Smile (band) · Wikipedia: Tom Skinner
years.h: Greenwood calls Skinner, Yorke joins months later
years.p: According to Wikipedia, [[Jonny Greenwood|e9fcfbbf-1743-4f73-8744-ada8da7394ea]] invited [[Tom Skinner|1d68b69c-ad5e-46c2-bede-4999dada10dd]] to work on musical ideas and [[Thom Yorke|8ed2e0b3-aa4c-4e13-bec3-dc7393ed4d6b]] came in a few months after.
years.xp:
The three agree not to give interviews about the project, so very little about its first years is on the record.

Wikipedia's Skinner page gives 2021 as the year he joined, which is when the band went public.

years.h: Glastonbury livestream: the debut, eight songs, no warning
years.p: The Smile play Live at Worthy Farm, filmed earlier that week. Yorke and Greenwood swap guitar, bass, Moog and Rhodes.
years.xp:
The eight songs include material from A Light for Attracting Attention before anyone outside the band has heard it.

Nigel Godrich, Radiohead's longtime producer, then produces the debut album. He cites the pandemic and Ed O'Brien's 2020 solo album Earth as factors in the project's emergence.

eras.title: A Light for Attracting Attention
eras.text: The debut arrives, and so do the reviews, the tour and a rank on Pitchfork's year-end list. Skinner's other band announces it's stopping in the same month the tour begins.

years.h: Three nights at Magazine London, played in the round
years.p: The first live shows debut "Speech Bubbles", "A Hairdryer" and "Waving a White Flag", and the band covers Joe Jackson's "It's Different for Girls".
years.xp: NME's James Balmont gave the shows 4 out of 5. The Guardian's Kitty Empire also gave 4 and said they were most convincing when they moved further from Radiohead; her colleague Alexis Petridis gave 3 and called it intriguing rather than dazzling.

yt: "You Will Never Work in Television Again"
years.h: "You Will Never Work in Television Again" is the first single
years.p: It arrives in January 2022, months after the Glastonbury livestream.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Light for Attracting Attention · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
years.h: A Light for Attracting Attention · XL Recordings
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.6 with Best New Music and ranked it No. 21 of 2022, and Metacritic scores it 86.
years.xp:
It's recorded in London with Nigel Godrich during 2020-21; Yorke sang from home during lockdown, logging on before his children came back from school. The cover painting is by Yorke and Stanley Donwood, done in gouache in Yorke's garden shed.

Pitchfork's Ryan Dombal called it the best album yet by a Radiohead side project. It debuts at No. 19 on the UK chart on digital release and climbs to No. 5 after the physical release on June 17.

years.h: A European and North American tour starts
years.p: It includes a July 2022 set at Montreux Jazz Festival, later released as a live album.

years.h: [[Sons of Kemet|fee950a2-e68c-4e76-b1ae-ff6efdf68b11]] announce they're closing the chapter
years.p: Skinner's jazz band stops "for the foreseeable future", two weeks into The Smile's tour.

eras.title: Wall of Eyes, Cutouts and a hospital
eras.text: With a new producer and Paul Thomas Anderson behind the cameras, The Smile record a second and third album from the same sessions.

years.h: "Bending Hectic" comes with a Paul Thomas Anderson video
years.p: The first single from the second album arrives in June 2023; the director of There Will Be Blood and Phantom Thread makes the videos.

years.h: Wall of Eyes · produced by Sam Petts-Davies
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Metacritic scores it 83; the London Contemporary Orchestra plays strings throughout.
years.xp:
It's recorded at Greenwood's Oxfordshire home studio and Abbey Road, beginning in March 2023. It peaks at No. 3 in the UK and Wikipedia reports it was the UK's highest-selling vinyl in its release week.

Anderson directs the videos for "Wall of Eyes" and "Friend of a Friend".

years.h: Greenwood is hospitalised, a European tour is cut short
years.p: Wikipedia reports a serious infection; parts of the August 2024 European tour are cancelled.

years.h: Cutouts · the third album from the same sessions
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and Metacritic scores it 82; Weirdcore makes the glitchy videos for every single.
years.xp: Yorke says splitting the material into two albums was to do it justice and avoid burnout. "Bodies Laughing" was written more than twenty years earlier and left unfinished until now.

eras.title: Back to the day job
eras.text: The Smile's two songwriters go back to Radiohead, but the band's still going.

years.h: Yorke and Greenwood rejoin [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]] for a European tour
years.p: It's the band's first tour in seven years, according to Wikipedia.
